name: M-2 Salt Range bridges and viaducts
assumptions: No photograph of this bridge from the side or below could be found, so the pier form is inferred: two chamfered rectangular columns under a cap beam for each carriageway. Esri shows only lit pier faces about 3 m wide at the middle joints; a single stem or wall pier would fit that too.
Pier and column dimensions (2.6 by 1.8 m columns, 11.6 by 1.9 by 1.5 m cap) are estimates.
Superstructure of five precast I girders 1.8 m deep under a 0.22 m slab is an estimate: Esri shows simply supported 29.9 m spans with joints at every pier, and no source gives the section.
Deck levels 557.5 m south and 558.5 m north read from the z15 terrain at the abutments; the deck is about 32 m above the 526 m valley floor by that terrain, not by a survey.
This is taken as the longest mapped bridge in the stretch; no source confirms that it is the 'highest pillared bridge' Wikipedia mentions, and the other mapped M-2 bridges are not modelled here.

Parapet shape, the pale median parapet on the deck, the ochre striped barrier on the approaches and the lane markings come from a road photo of another short bridge in the same Salt Range section, not this bridge.
Outer strip colour and the width split of pale and dark surface are read from Esri tiles at about 0.5 m per pixel.
Column foundations continue 2 m below the sampled ground so that terrain differences do not expose them; footings are not modelled.
suppress is empty on purpose: the dossier footprint is a line along a 30 m deep valley, and flattening the ground under it would cut the valley sides.
No night lighting: no source describes any.
